To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a new class of potent and cell permeant inhibitors of ubiquitin-proteasome system that do not inhibit the proteasome and selectively kills cervical cancer cells.
we identified a new class of chemical inhibitors of ubiquitination that selectively kills cervical cancer cells by targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome system.

(1) we identified a new class of small molecule inhibitors of the ubiquitin-proteasome system that are distinct from the 20S inhibitors and (2) these inhibitors trigger cell death in cervical cancer cells by inducing the formation of toxic aggregates and by blocking their degradation in lysosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel chemical probes that selectively inhibit the ubiquitin-proteasome system and that may be used as a basis for the development of new anticancer therapies for cervical cancer.

the development and evaluation of a new class chemical inhibitors of the ubiquitin-dependent proteasome system, and the discovery of a lead compound, RAMB1, which selectively targets cervical cancer cells.

identifying and characterizing new classes of small molecule inhibitors of ubiquitin-proteasome system that selectively kill cervical cancer cells, thus providing the rationale for the design of new anticancer agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

RAMB1 is a novel chemical inhibitor of ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) that selectively targets cervical cancer cells and synergistically enhances cell death when combined with lysosomal inhibition.
RAMB1 inhibiting the ubiquitin-proteasome system selectively induces cell death of cervical and other cancer cells.

the chalcone-based chemical inhibitors described herein, including RAMB1, are potent inhibitors of ubiquitin-proteasome dependent protein degradation that can be used as a new class of anticancer agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RAMB1 is a promising candidate for cervical cancer therapy.
the chalcone-based chemical inhibitor, RAMB1, selectively kills cervical cancer cells by interfering with ubiquitination-dependent protein degradation and lysosomal degradation pathways.

we have developed an innovative strategy to target cervical cancer cells through a combination of proteasome inhibition with the 20S inhibitor Bortezomid, and lysosome inhibition with the lysosome inhibitors Chloroquine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cervical cancer cells are particularly sensitive to inhibition of ubiquitin-proteasome system without 20S proteolytic inhibition, and that the combination of RAMB1 and a lysosome inhibitor is a potent therapeutic strategy for cervical cancer.

the 20S core proteasome catalytic activities do not have to be inhibited to kill cancer cells, and the 26S proteasome can be targeted by small molecules without inhibiting the 20S catalytic activities.
targeting the ubiquitin-proteasome system without compromising the catalytical activity of the 20 S proteasome is a novel and promising approach to selectively kill cervical cancer cells.
